newsitem.title: ITALY: Montedison sees better margins in H2 1996.
newsitem.headline: Montedison sees better margins in H2 1996.

text.p: Italian agro-industrial group Montedison said it expected positive 1996 results with second half gross operating profit higher than the first six months.
Managing Director Enrico Bondi told a shareholders meeting he was confident forecasts made for the full year when the interim results were published in September would be realised.

For the six months to end-June, Montedison reported consolidated net profit of 108 billion lire against 1.09 trillion lire in the year-ago period, when Montedison made exceptional capital gains from the transfer to Montell of its plastics activities.
Group gross operating profit was 1.62 trillion lire against 1.93 trillion.
It said at the time it expected an improvement in results for the second half of 1996 given a positive trend in revenues seen between May and August.
It also expected a fall in debt and financial charges due to income of 448 billion lire in tax credits in July and August.
Tuesday's meeting approved measures which formally settled a dispute reaching back to 1993 with auditors Price Waterhouse.
Under terms of the settlement, the auditors agreed to pay 31 billion lire to Montedison and 20 billion lire to its controlling company Compart, formerly known as Ferruzzi Finanziaria.
Price Waterhouse has said the payments were not an acknowledgement of responsibility.

Both Ferruzzi and Montedison went to the brink of collapse in 1993 following the discovery of huge debts. The companies are still controlled by a group of creditor banks which salvaged them at the time.
Price Waterhouse was the auditor in the years leading up to the collapse. -- Milan newsroom +392 66129589
